evals.prompt: I need to reproduce ticket PS-9999 on Percona Server 8.4.5 with async replication, source plus one replica.
evals.expected_output: A namespace-scoped deploy command pinned to ps:8.4.5 (not :latest), a brief node layout (node0 source / node1 replica), a verification command using `show replica status\G`, and a namespace-scoped teardown.
expectations: Pins to exact patch ps:8.4.5, NOT ps:8.4 or ps:latest
Uses --namespace=PS-9999 (or similar ticket-derived name), NOT the default namespace
First node has no master= ; second node has master=node0
Verification uses `anydbver exec node1 -- mysql` (or equivalent) to run `show replica status\G`
Teardown uses `anydbver --namespace=PS-9999 destroy`, NOT bare `anydbver destroy`
States the prereq check (anydbver --version / docker reachable) before showing the deploy command
Does NOT propose --keep (this is a fresh repro)

evals.prompt: Spin up a 3-node Percona XtraDB Cluster on 8.4 and put sysbench OLTP load against it.
evals.expected_output: A single deploy command with one PXC bootstrap node and two `master=node0,galera` joiners, plus a sysbench node pointed at one of them; verification via `wsrep_cluster_size` and a sysbench prepare/run.
expectations: First node uses pxc:8.4 with NO master= (bootstrap)
Subsequent nodes use master=node0,galera (or chained through node1)
sysbench node uses sysbench:latest,mysql=nodeN where nodeN is one of the PXC nodes
Verification includes `show status like 'wsrep_cluster_size'`
Mentions that wsrep_cluster_size should equal 3
Does NOT add unnecessary keywords like docker-image (PXC bug-repro should run from packages)

evals.prompt: Async replication chain (3 MySQL nodes), with ProxySQL in front and Orchestrator watching the topology.
evals.expected_output: A 4-node deploy: ps source on node0, two ps replicas chained, Orchestrator on its own node with `master=node0`, and ProxySQL either on its own node or fronting the chain via `percona-proxysql:latest,master=node0`.
expectations: node0 has ps:8.4 (or pinned patch) with NO master=
node1 has master=node0 ; node2 has master=node1 (chained) OR master=node0 (fan-out — both valid)
percona-orchestrator:latest,master=node0 lives on a dedicated node
percona-proxysql:latest,master=node0 lives on a dedicated node OR is added to an existing node
Verification mentions opening Orchestrator UI / inspecting ProxySQL `mysql_servers` table
Does NOT use --provider=kubectl (this is bare-Docker)

evals.prompt: Reproducir un bug en PostgreSQL 18.1 con replicación lógica entre primary y standby.
evals.expected_output: Comando de deploy con namespace dedicado, pg:18.1 fijado en patch exacto, ambos nodos con `wal=logical`, y un paso de verificación que consulte `pg_stat_wal_receiver` / `pg_replication_slots`.
expectations: Pin exacto en pg:18.1 (no pg:18 ni pg:latest)
Usa --namespace=<algo descriptivo> (ticket id o similar)
Ambos nodos tienen wal=logical
El standby usa primary=node0 (o master=node0 — ambos válidos en PG)
Verificación menciona pg_stat_wal_receiver O pg_replication_slots
Teardown usa el mismo --namespace=<nombre>
Responde apropiadamente al prompt en español (no asume inglés)

evals.prompt: Full Patroni HA stack on Percona PG 17 — 3 Patroni members, HAProxy-Patroni, and pgbouncer in front.
evals.expected_output: A 5-node deploy: 3 Patroni members on cluster=cluster1, a haproxy-patroni node listing the 3 members positionally, and a pgbouncer node pointing at the HAProxy node. Verification via `patronictl list` and a query through pgbouncer.
expectations: Uses ppg:17 (Percona PG), not pg:17 (vanilla)
All Patroni members share the same cluster=cluster1 (or whatever name)
haproxy-patroni uses the positional `node0,node1,node2` form (NO equals sign for the node list)
pgbouncer points at the HAProxy node (positional list or master=)
Verification includes `patronictl list` from one of the Patroni members
Mentions that one of node0/node1/node2 will be elected leader (others are sync/async standbys)

evals.prompt: Patroni cluster with pgbackrest writing backups to MinIO. Show me how to take a backup and verify it.
evals.expected_output: A deploy that includes `minio:docker-image` on a dedicated node (or shared node), a Patroni cluster, and `pgbackrest:s3=nodeN` on the PG nodes; verification via `pgbackrest --stanza=main info`.
expectations: MinIO is deployed with docker-image (it's the supported way for MinIO)
pgbackrest uses s3=nodeN where nodeN is the MinIO node
Patroni members each have pgbackrest configured (not just one)
Includes a `pgbackrest --stanza=main backup` step (or notes that pgbackrest auto-takes one)
Verification uses `pgbackrest --stanza=main info`
Does NOT confuse s3=nodeN with server=nodeN (those are different keywords used by different tools)

evals.prompt: Spin up a PSMDB 8.0 sharded cluster — 2 shards × 3 nodes, 3 config servers, 1 mongos.
evals.expected_output: First the keyfile-copy commands (openssl + cp loop for cfg0-keyfile to rs0/rs1-keyfile), THEN the deploy with role=shard / role=cfg / mongos-cfg + mongos-shard. Verification via `sh.status()` on the mongos.
expectations: Includes `openssl rand -base64 756 > secret/cfg0-keyfile` BEFORE the deploy command
Includes `cp -L secret/cfg0-keyfile secret/rs0-keyfile` AND `cp -L secret/cfg0-keyfile secret/rs1-keyfile` (one per shard RS)
Each shard node has replica-set=rsN,role=shard ; each cfg node has replica-set=cfg0,role=cfg
Only the FIRST mongos has both mongos-cfg: and mongos-shard:
mongos-shard: lists shards as rs0/n0,n1,n2,rs1/n3,n4,n5 (RS-name/node-list groups)
Verification uses `sh.status()` from node9 (mongos), not from a shard primary
Pins to psmdb:8.0 explicitly

evals.prompt: 3-node PSMDB replica set with Percona Backup for MongoDB, backups going to MinIO.
evals.expected_output: A deploy with MinIO on node0, three PSMDB replica-set nodes each carrying `pbm:latest,s3=node0/backup`. Verification via `pbm status` showing all three RS members have agents.
expectations: MinIO uses docker-image
Every PSMDB node (all 3) has pbm:latest,s3=node0/backup — NOT just one
Replica set: first node has replica-set=rs0 ; subsequent have replica-set=rs0,master=node1 (or master=node0)
Verification uses `pbm status` (showing all 3 agents are connected)
s3 path is node0/backup (or node0 with default bucket)
PBM agent must be running on each node — eval should mention or verify this

evals.prompt: I want one PMM 3.x server monitoring a Percona Server node, a Postgres node, and a PSMDB replica set node, all in the same lab.
evals.expected_output: A multi-node deploy: pmm:3.7.0,docker-image,port=12443 on node0, then ps/pg/psmdb on node1/2/3 each carrying pmm-client:3.7.0-7,server=node0:8443. Verification: open https://localhost:12443 and run `pmm-admin list` on each client.
expectations: PMM client uses server=node0:8443 — NOT server=node0 (that's PMM 2.x), NOT server=node0:443
pmm-client version includes the release suffix `-7`: pmm-client:3.7.0-7 — NOT bare pmm-client:3.7.0
PMM server has docker-image modifier
Host port for the UI is set via port=12443 (or any free port)
All three monitored nodes (PS, PG, PSMDB) share the same server=node0:8443 string
Verification mentions the host-side URL (https://localhost:12443) and `pmm-admin list`
Does NOT confuse host port (12443) with internal port (8443) — explanation should make this clear if asked

evals.prompt: Local k8s with the Percona PG operator — primary cluster plus a standby cluster in another namespace.
evals.expected_output: A k3d-based deploy: k3d, cert-manager, k8s-pg:2.7.0, then a second k8s-pg:2.7.0,namespace=pgo1,standby. Verification via `kubectl get pg --all-namespaces` and entering `anydbver shell` for kubectl.
expectations: Includes k3d (or k3d:latest) — needed to bootstrap the nested cluster
Includes cert-manager (the Percona PG operator requires it)
First k8s-pg deploys to the default namespace; second uses namespace=pgo1,standby
Mentions that `anydbver shell` enters a container with kubectl/helm pre-wired
Verification command uses kubectl (e.g. `kubectl get pg -A`)
RAM warning: cert-manager + operator + 3-replica CR ≈ 6–8 GB (or similar caveat)
Does NOT use bare-Docker keywords like `pg:18` (this is operator territory)

evals.prompt: I deployed a PSMDB sharded cluster but mongos refuses to add shards with errors about cluster IDs. What went wrong and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the missing keyfile-copy step as the root cause (every RS must share the same keyfile). Recovery: destroy the namespace, regenerate cfg0-keyfile with openssl, copy to rs0-keyfile / rs1-keyfile / rs2-keyfile, then redeploy.
expectations: Identifies keyfile mismatch as the root cause (NOT a network or version problem)
References that every replica set in the cluster must share the same keyfile
Recovery includes destroying the existing namespace BEFORE regenerating keyfiles (because keyfiles are persisted in secret/)
Includes `openssl rand -base64 756 > secret/cfg0-keyfile`
Includes the cp loop for rs0-keyfile, rs1-keyfile, rs2-keyfile
Does NOT propose to fix in place — keyfile state requires destroy + redeploy
Does NOT suggest unrelated fixes (network, mongos config, version pinning)

evals.prompt: I'm reproducing a Percona Server 8.4.5 bug across many destroy+redeploy iterations. Speed up the loop with `install` + `cache:`.
evals.expected_output: Two passes: first deploy `install ps:8.4.5 cache:ps-8.4.5` to bake the cache, then a second deploy with `install ps:8.4.5 cache:ps-8.4.5` per node followed by `ps:8.4.5` per node (the configure-and-start step). Subsequent destroys/redeploys reuse the cached image.
expectations: First command is the cache-build pass: `anydbver deploy install ps:8.4.5 cache:ps-8.4.5`
Second command repeats `install ps:8.4.5 cache:ps-8.4.5` on EACH node (one line per node)
Second command has a SEPARATE `default ps:8.4.5` / `node1 ps:8.4.5 master=...` (or master:default) section to actually configure-and-start
Cache name is consistent (cache:ps-8.4.5) across all references — NOT a different name on each node
Pinned to ps:8.4.5 (the bug-repro version) throughout — not :latest
Mentions that `anydbver destroy --remove-cache` wipes the cache when done

evals.prompt: Patroni cluster with pgbackrest, but I want all 3 nodes sharing the same backup repo over NFS instead of S3.
evals.expected_output: A deploy with `nfs` on node0, then 3 Patroni nodes each carrying pg, patroni, `pgbackrest:repo=/mnt/nfs/pgbackrest`, and `nfs-client:server=node0`. Verification: `pgbackrest --stanza=main info` from any Patroni node + `mount | grep nfs` on a client.
expectations: node0 has the `nfs` keyword (alias for nfs-server)
Each Patroni member (node1/2/3) has nfs-client:server=node0
pgbackrest uses repo=/mnt/nfs/pgbackrest (the shared NFS path), NOT s3=node0
Patroni members chain via master=node1 (after node1 bootstraps) or all use master=node0
Notes the destroy-order gotcha: tear down clients BEFORE the NFS server, otherwise Docker wedges
Notes that the NFS export is tmpfs-backed and ephemeral — fine for repro but data is lost on teardown
Verification uses `pgbackrest --stanza=main info` AND `mount | grep nfs` on a client

evals.prompt: I want to reproduce a PMM HA Tech Preview issue locally on my laptop (8 cores, 16GB RAM). What's the smallest working setup?
evals.expected_output: A single command `anydbver deploy k3d k8s-pmm-ha:1.4.1` (which defaults to size=small), plus how to access the UI via HAProxy port-forward, and the verification that 3 PMM pods are running with Raft leader election in place.
expectations: Uses `k3d k8s-pmm-ha:1.4.1` (or `k8s-pmm-ha:1.4.1,size=small`) — does NOT pass size=full on a laptop
Mentions the default profile keeps PMM at 3 replicas for Raft HA but shrinks every backend (HAProxy, PG, pgBouncer, VictoriaMetrics) to 1 replica and ClickHouse to 2
Calls out that PMM HA is Tech Preview — not production-ready
UI access via `kubectl port-forward -n pmm svc/pmm-ha-haproxy 8443:443` then https://localhost:8443
Default login is admin / admin (or whatever password= was set to)
Verification includes `kubectl get pods -n pmm -l app.kubernetes.io/name=pmm-ha` (3 pmm-ha-N pods Ready)
Mentions that only the Raft leader returns 200 on /v1/server/leaderHealthCheck (HAProxy routes to it)
Does NOT suggest pulling pmm-ha:latest — pins to 1.4.1 (PMM 3.7.1)

evals.prompt: Levantar CloudNativePG en local con k3d: un solo nodo Postgres 17, un poco mas de disco, para probar una extension.
evals.expected_output: A single command `anydbver deploy k3d k8s-cnpg:1.30.0,replicas=1,db-version=17,storage=5Gi`, plus verification via kubectl and the note that the operator itself lands in cnpg-system, not the cluster namespace.
expectations: Includes k3d (or k3d:latest) to bootstrap the nested cluster
Uses the k8s-cnpg keyword (alias cnpg / cloudnative-pg-operator) — NOT k8s-pg, which is the Percona operator
replicas=1 for a single instance — explains that replicas= is the TOTAL instance count for CNPG (1 primary + N-1 replicas), unlike the Percona operators
db-version=17 to pin PostgreSQL 17 (ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:17); without it you get the operator default
storage=5Gi for the per-instance PVC (default is 1Gi)
Does NOT add cert-manager as a hard requirement (CloudNativePG does not need it the way k8s-pg does)
Mentions the operator always runs in the cnpg-system namespace and watches all namespaces, so namespace= places the Cluster only
Verification uses kubectl (e.g. `kubectl get cluster -A` and `kubectl -n cnpg get pods`), reached via `anydbver shell`
Does NOT promise PMM or MinIO integration — those are skipped with a warning for CloudNativePG

evals.prompt: Necesito reproducir algo en Crunchy Postgres para Kubernetes, la version 5.8, un solo instance en PG 17. Se puede con anydbver?
evals.expected_output: A single command `anydbver deploy k3d k8s-crunchy:5.8.8,replicas=1,db-version=17`, plus kubectl verification and the note that the operator lands in the postgres-operator namespace, not the cluster one.
expectations: Includes k3d (or k3d:latest) to bootstrap the nested cluster
Uses the k8s-crunchy keyword (alias crunchy / crunchy-postgres-operator) — NOT k8s-pg, which is the Percona fork, and NOT k8s-cnpg
replicas=1 for a single instance — explains that replicas= is the TOTAL instance count, default 3
db-version=17 sets spec.postgresVersion, and only majors the operator ships an image for (15 to 18) are accepted
Says the operator always runs in the postgres-operator namespace and watches every namespace, so namespace= places the PostgresCluster
Verification with kubectl get postgrescluster -A / kubectl -n crunchy get pods, and psql inside the -c database container
Does NOT claim PMM integration works with Crunchy (MinIO backups do work, PMM does not)

evals.prompt: I want to test a Crunchy Postgres for Kubernetes cluster whose pgBackRest backups go to MinIO, and I need to reach the database from my laptop. Can anydbver set that up?
evals.expected_output: A single deploy command combining k8s-minio (with certs=self-signed), cert-manager and k8s-crunchy with expose, plus how to check the backup with pgbackrest info and where the LoadBalancer address shows up.
expectations: Includes k3d to bootstrap the nested cluster
Deploys k8s-minio and k8s-crunchy in the SAME command, with k8s-minio before the operator keyword
Adds cert-manager and certs=self-signed, and explains TLS is REQUIRED: pgBackRest only talks to S3 over HTTPS, so a plain HTTP MinIO is skipped with a warning
Explains that MinIO becomes pgBackRest repo1 while repo2 stays a local volume, and that PGO's replica-create backup lands in the bucket right away
Uses expose on the k8s-crunchy keyword and says it puts <cluster>-ha on a LoadBalancer while -replicas and -pgbouncer get NodePorts, and that -primary is headless
Verification with pgbackrest info --stanza=db inside the pgbackrest-dedicated repo host pod, and kubectl get svc for the LoadBalancer addresses
Does NOT invent a backup= or schedule= option, and does NOT claim PMM works with Crunchy
